sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cathubodua is a battle goddess of the Gauls. Her worship is recorded in the Haute-Savoie region of what is now France. The tribal surname Boduogenos, which means people of Bodua, preserves her name. Writers have connected her to the war goddess Badb. Women dressed in black, acting as druids, imitated the Badb in the thick of fighting, yelling from the sidelines to stir the men to bolder deeds; such was the sight when the druidic school on Anglesey met its ruin. Whether Badb and her fellow goddesses of war began as Celtic figures or stem from an earlier, pre-Celtic layer remains a matter of argument. Most scholars think her bird shape reaches back to an unnamed goddess of the Neolithic age who was commonly drawn in that form.
